data.description: Upgrade rp_build from a one-shot LLM call to an agent-powered plan generation process that can explore the codebase, and leverage the project indexer to inject real code context into plan generation. The goal is to close the quality gap between plans generated by riotplan CLI and plans generated through Cursor, by giving rp_build the same codebase awareness that Cursor has.

data.content:
The user has been building out the riotplan explore CLI command and discovered a significant quality gap between plans generated through Cursor (which have full codebase access) and plans generated through rp_build (which makes a single one-shot LLM call with only plan artifacts as context).

Specific comparison: The riotplan-command-line plan (Cursor-generated) names specific files like execution/src/index.ts, references actual classes like ConversationManager and AgentLoop, has concrete tasks like "Add tools parameter to the Request interface", and includes Key Files and Dependencies sections. The riotplan-format plan (rp_build-generated) has placeholder "Files Changed" sections, abstract conceptual tasks, no Key Files or Dependencies sections, and reads like a consultant who never saw the code.

Root cause: rp_build in generator.ts makes a single provider.execute() call (now streaming via executeStream) with only IDEA.md, SHAPING.md, constraints, questions, and evidence summaries in the prompt. It has NO tools, NO iteration, and NO codebase context.

The user wants two things:
1. Make rp_build agent-powered - use the AgentLoop with file-reading tools so the LLM can explore the codebase while drafting the plan
2. Leverage the project indexer (which takes ~500ms) to inject real code context into plan generation

Additionally, the project already has a working index_project tool that scans files, packages, and exports, and a query_index tool for fast lookups. These were built specifically to reduce LLM round-trips by providing local, queryable project structure data.

data.constraint: Must reuse the existing AgentLoop from @kjerneverk/agentic - no new agent framework
Must use the existing project indexer (index_project/query_index) for codebase awareness - not build a new one
Generated plans must include concrete file paths, class/interface names, and method references - not placeholders like "_List files that will be modified..._"
Must maintain backward compatibility with the existing rp_build MCP tool interface - same parameters, same output files (SUMMARY.md, EXECUTION_PLAN.md, STATUS.md, PROVENANCE.md, plan/*.md)
The agent-powered build should give read-only codebase access (read_file, list_files, grep, query_index) - no write access to project files during plan generation
The project index should be built automatically before plan generation starts, taking no more than ~500ms for typical projects
Must work both in CLI (riotplan explore → rp_build) and MCP server contexts - the build tool should detect available tools and use agent mode when file tools are available

data.note: Two-pronged approach: (1) Auto-inject project index context into the generation prompt as a new == CODEBASE CONTEXT == section - this is cheap and gets immediate value. (2) Replace one-shot generation with agent-powered generation using AgentLoop + read-only file tools - this enables the LLM to explore code interactively during plan creation.

The agent-powered build should use a new system prompt tailored for plan generation that instructs the LLM to: (1) explore the codebase using tools, (2) identify relevant files, interfaces, and patterns, (3) draft the plan with concrete references, (4) output structured JSON matching the existing GeneratedPlan interface.

For the agent-powered approach, the plan output could be collected via a special `write_plan` tool that the agent calls when ready, rather than trying to parse a massive JSON blob from the text stream. This is cleaner and avoids JSON parsing issues.

The existing `findProjectRoot()` in common.ts already walks up from plan path to find package.json - this same logic should be reused in rp_build to know where to index. The index is already cached in memory so if explore already indexed it, rp_build gets it for free.

data.name: Agent-Powered Build with Index Injection
data.description: Replace the one-shot generatePlan() call with a two-phase approach: (1) Before generation, auto-build the project index and inject a CODEBASE CONTEXT section into the prompt with package list, key files, and exported interfaces. (2) Replace the single LLM call with an AgentLoop session that has read-only file tools (read_file, list_files, grep, query_index) plus a special write_plan tool. The agent explores the codebase, reads relevant files, and builds the plan iteratively. The write_plan tool accepts the GeneratedPlan JSON structure and signals completion. The existing buildPlan() in build.ts orchestrates this: loads artifacts, indexes project, creates agent loop, runs it, collects plan from write_plan result, then writes all output files (SUMMARY.md, etc.) exactly as before.
tradeoffs: Pro: Plans will reference actual files, interfaces, and code patterns
Pro: Reuses existing AgentLoop and tool infrastructure
Pro: Index injection is cheap (~500ms) and provides immediate context
Pro: write_plan tool avoids JSON parsing issues from text stream
Pro: Backward compatible - same output files, same MCP interface
Con: Agent-powered generation takes longer (3-5 min vs 30 sec for one-shot)
Con: More token consumption per plan generation
Con: Need to handle agent iteration limits and potential failures gracefully
Con: Two code paths - agent mode when tools available, fallback to one-shot when not
assumptions: AgentLoop can be used programmatically without a terminal/interactive session
Read-only file tools are sufficient - the agent doesn't need to write during exploration
The project indexer cache persists across the explore → build transition within a CLI session
A write_plan tool can cleanly collect structured JSON output from the agent

data.reason: This is the only approach that addresses both user requirements (agent-powered build + index integration) while reusing existing infrastructure. The tradeoffs of longer generation time and more tokens are acceptable because plan quality is the primary goal.
Plan built from shaping stage with 5 steps, generated through Cursor with full codebase awareness

data.note: The end goal is IDE independence: `riotplan explore` from a bare terminal should produce the same quality plan as using RiotPlan through Cursor with Opus. The full lifecycle (explore → shape → build) must work end-to-end without an IDE. The build step is the biggest quality gap, but the entire flow needs to be validated as a standalone experience.

Model quality matters. Cursor uses Opus (high-end model). The CLI currently defaults to claude-sonnet-4-20250514. For plan generation specifically, we should consider using a more capable model (opus) since plan quality is the primary output and this is a one-time cost per plan. The explore conversation can stay on sonnet, but rp_build might benefit from opus-level reasoning.

Critical architecture insight: the explore agent already has read_file, grep, query_index tools. But when it calls rp_build, that tool runs a separate one-shot LLM call that has NONE of those tools. The fix is to make rp_build's internal generation inherit tools from its calling context. The tool execution context in wrapper.ts (line 133-158) passes workingDirectory but not the available tools. We need to thread tools through or detect them from the CLI environment.

data.constraint: Must be language-agnostic - the project indexer and codebase context must work for Python, Rust, Java, C/C++, Go, Ruby, Swift, and .NET projects, not just Node.js/TypeScript
